for(chipType in chipTypes) {

ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(glad)

This is what I suspected.  When merging two CN estimates from two
different chip types, the Aroma framework uses the names of the
arrays/files to figure out which goes together.   More precisely, it
pairs them up based on the information that getNames() of the two
chip-type data sets returns, which in your case is:

Mapping250K_Nsp: AA-HGG024-250knsp, AA-HGG045-250knsp, AA-HGG052-250knsp, ...,
Mapping250K_Sty: AA-HGG024-250ksty, AA-HGG045-250ksty, AA-HGG052-250ksty, ...,

Although it is clear to you as a human being that AA-HGG024-250knsp
and AA-HGG024-250ksty should be coupled, there is no way Aroma can
resolve that.  If they would have been named with comma-separated tags
from the beginning it would have worked out of the box, e.g.

Mapping250K_Nsp: AA-HGG024,250knsp, AA-HGG045,250knsp, AA-HGG052,250knsp, ...,
Mapping250K_Sty: AA-HGG024,250ksty, AA-HGG045,250ksty, AA-HGG052,250ksty, ...,

because the *name* parts would match up (and tags would be ignored), i.e.

Mapping250K_Nsp: AA-HGG024, AA-HGG045, AA-HGG052, ...,
Mapping250K_Sty: AA-HGG024, AA-HGG045, AA-HGG052, ...,

In your case, the easiest is to just attach a so called fullnames
translator to each of the two data sets, e.g.

setFullNamesTranslator(cesNList[[1]]), fnt);
setFullNamesTranslator(cesNList[[2]]), fnt);

where fnt is a *function* that takes a vector of names as the first
argument, i.e.

fnt <- function(names, ...) {
  # Here you can modify the content of 'names' using for instance gsub().
  names <- gsub(..., names);
  names;
}

After doing this you should get:

> str(getFullNames(cesNList[[1]]))
>  chr [1:121] "AA-HGG024,total" "AA-HGG045,total" ...
> str(getFullNames(cesNList[[2]]))
>  chr [1:121] "AA-HGG024,total" "AA-HGG045,total" ...

Recreating the GladModel object, you should get something like:

> print(nbrOfArrays(glad))
> [1] 121
> strt(getArrays(glad));
>  chr [1:121] "AA-HGG024" "AA-HGG045" ...

Finally, yes, it is odd that getArrays(glad) currently returns an
empty vector; I would have expected it to return a vector of 2*121
elements.  It seems to be a bug; I'll add it to my todo list.

Hope this helps

/Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Thu, Nov 3, 2011 at 8:20 AM, <qian...@suregene.net> wrote:
>
>
> Hello,
> I am using my SNP6.0 data to run the code in CRMA v2 vignette. The following step is very slow, but I couldn't find how "units" calculated here in the if { } was used in the following step. Would you please explain the purpose of the following code and how it is used later? Thank you.
>
> Qian
>
> if (length(findUnitsTodo(plm)) > 0) {
>   # Fit CN probes quickly (~5-10s/array + some overhead)
>   units <- fitCnProbes(plm, verbose=verbose)
>   str(units)
>   # int [1:945826] 935590 935591 935592 935593 935594 935595 ...
>
>   # Fit remaining units, i.e. SNPs (~5-10min/array)
>   units <- fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
>   str(units)
> }

If understand you correctly, your question is "why is that chunk of
code needed if all that is returned is a vector of integers ('units')
which is not used in any of the code (not shown) following?"

It is true that 'units' object is not used later.  We could even add a
'rm(units)' at the end to make this even more explicit.  it is there
only for the purpose of displaying which CDF units are processed in
fitCnProbes() and fit().  In other words, from an data processing
point of view, you can just do:

if (length(findUnitsTodo(plm)) > 0) {
  fitCnProbes(plm, verbose=verbose);
  fit(plm, verbose=verbose);
}

At guess at this point your question becomes, "but nothing is returned
by those functions, so why even bother running them?".  This is where
the Aroma framework is fundamentally different from what you see in
most other R packages: Each of those two functions processes the data
and saves the results to files.  When you in the next step of the
script do:

ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm);

those results that were written to file are picked up.  (Technically
nothing is loaded from file; instead 'ces' will point to those files
internally and only when the data is really needed it is loaded, but
all that are technical details).

Finally, since results are stored in files, it means that they will
still be there if you restart R and/or restart your computer.  The
Aroma framework, and more specifically, fitCnProbes() and fit() will
detect this and simply skip already processed results.  To avoid
having to do this check twice, we help Aroma out by testing
(length(findUnitsTodo(plm)) > 0), but it is not really needed, so you
could have done:

fitCnProbes(plm, verbose=verbose);
fit(plm, verbose=verbose);
ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm);

Now to the "very slow" comment: It is not clear how many samples you
are processing, but for your information, the fitCnProbes() method is
optimized to process the single-probe non-polymorphic copy-number
probes on the GenomeWideSNP_6 array, so that is as fast as it can be.
The fit() method was designed to be able to process data from any chip
type together with any type of CDF so it could not be optimized
equally well.  fit() is what takes most of the time here.  The upside
is that you can process virtually any number of arrays without having
to worry about memory issues.  Also, if you try to reanalyze the same
arrays again, your results will be instantaneously available from
file.

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v2.3.0 released
messages.subject_clean: aroma.affymetrix v2.3.0 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
aroma.affymetrix v2.3.0 and friends have been released.  Update by running:

source("http://aroma-project.org/hbLite.R");
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix");

The is a rather small release - the main update is that now all
aroma.* packages have a namespace.  This should not affect an end user
much, except that it should improve the stability of the code, and
lower the risk for unforeseeable bugs.  Other than that, there are few
new methods available (see below).  I still strongly recommend an
update.

/Henrik

o Added a namespace to the package, which will be more or less
  a requirement starting with R v2.14.0.

  of suggested package, just to remove one R CMD check "NOTE".

Version: 2.2.3 [2011-09-29]
o Added more system tests.

Version: 2.2.2 [2011-09-17]
o Added writeCdfByExcludingCells() for AffymetrixCdfFile.

Version: 2.2.1 [2011-09-11]
o Added createExonByTranscriptCdf() for creating exon-by-transcript CDFs.
  This methods was adapted from the createTranscriptCDF(), which was
  previously provided online.
o Added a build script for createExonByTranscriptCdf() on HuEx-1_0-st-v2.
o Added getHeaderAttributes() for AffymetrixNetAffxCsvFile which is
  used by new getGenomeBuild(), getNetAffxBuild() and getNetAffxDate().

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

o Added a namespace to the package, which will be more or less
  a requirement starting with R v2.14.0.

Version: 2.2.2 [2011-09-29]
o Added alpha version of the AromaRepository class.

Version: 2.2.1 [2011-09-24]
o readHeader(), readRawFooter() and writeRawFooter() of
  AromaTabularBinaryFile would try to read non-signed 4-byte integers,
  which is not supported and would instead be read as signed integers.
  From R v2.13.1 this would generated warnings.

> Henrik Bengtsson <henrik.b...@aroma-project.org> Nov 01 03:25PM -0700
>
> Hi.
>
>> [1] 0
>> =========== print(getArrays(glad));  ===============
>> character(0)
>
> This is what I suspected. When merging two CN estimates from two
> different chip types, the Aroma framework uses the names of the
> arrays/files to figure out which goes together. More precisely, it
> pairs them up based on the information that getNames() of the two
> chip-type data sets returns, which in your case is:
>
> Mapping250K_Nsp: AA-HGG024-250knsp, AA-HGG045-250knsp, AA-HGG052-250knsp,
> ...,
> Mapping250K_Sty: AA-HGG024-250ksty, AA-HGG045-250ksty, AA-HGG052-250ksty,
> ...,
>
> Although it is clear to you as a human being that AA-HGG024-250knsp
> and AA-HGG024-250ksty should be coupled, there is no way Aroma can
> resolve that. If they would have been named with comma-separated tags
> from the beginning it would have worked out of the box, e.g.
>
> Mapping250K_Nsp: AA-HGG024,250knsp, AA-HGG045,250knsp, AA-HGG052,250knsp,
> ...,
> Mapping250K_Sty: AA-HGG024,250ksty, AA-HGG045,250ksty, AA-HGG052,250ksty,
> ...,
>
> because the *name* parts would match up (and tags would be ignored), i.e.
>
> Mapping250K_Nsp: AA-HGG024, AA-HGG045, AA-HGG052, ...,
> Mapping250K_Sty: AA-HGG024, AA-HGG045, AA-HGG052, ...,
>
> In your case, the easiest is to just attach a so called fullnames
> translator to each of the two data sets, e.g.
>
> setFullNamesTranslator(cesNList[[1]]), fnt);
> setFullNamesTranslator(cesNList[[2]]), fnt);
>
> where fnt is a *function* that takes a vector of names as the first
> argument, i.e.
>
> fnt <- function(names, ...) {
> # Here you can modify the content of 'names' using for instance gsub().
> names <- gsub(..., names);
> names;
> }
>
> After doing this you should get:
>
>>  chr [1:121] "AA-HGG024,total" "AA-HGG045,total" ...
>> str(getFullNames(cesNList[[2]]))
>>  chr [1:121] "AA-HGG024,total" "AA-HGG045,total" ...
>
> Recreating the GladModel object, you should get something like:
>
>> [1] 121
>> strt(getArrays(glad));
>>  chr [1:121] "AA-HGG024" "AA-HGG045" ...
>
> Finally, yes, it is odd that getArrays(glad) currently returns an
> empty vector; I would have expected it to return a vector of 2*121
> elements. It seems to be a bug; I'll add it to my todo list.
>
> Hope this helps
>
> /Henrik

On Sat, Nov 5, 2011 at 4:06 PM, Les Ander <les...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Henrik,
> I am completely new to R and to aroma;
> I've looked here http://www.aroma-project.org/howtos
> but did not get the answer to my question.
>
> Following your excellent documents I have been able to get the
> ds <-
> doCRMAv2("mycellfiles",chipType="GenomeWideSNP_6,Full",verbose=-10)
> run successfully.

First of all, "mycellfiles" is not a very useful name for a data set.
It will help you later if you pick a good name from the beginning.  I
tend to name them by for instance investigators name and year, e.g.
"DoeJ_2011".

>
> Now, I am not sure how to go about :
>
> 1. Printing out the Copy number calls into a text file.

Please be aware that CN segmentation and CN calling are two different
things are the latter is a much more complicated problem than the
former.

> I am not sure if I still need to do segmentation separately. And if
> yes, what command I should use.

I've just created the 'Total copy-number segmentation (non-paired
CBS)' vignette:

 http://aroma-project.org/vignettes/NonPairedCBS

See if that provides what you need.

>
> Ideally I would like to know something like this for each cnv region
> my_cellfile_1 chr1 1001 4001 cnstate=3
> my_cellfile_2 chr19 20   340  cnstate=1

Here you indicate that you wish to call the CN state of each segments.
 As indicated in the above vignette, it is only a few CN segmentation
models that also call CN states.  In aroma it is only the GLAD method
(GladModel) that does that, but be aware that it may be too slow for
high-density arrays such as GenomeWideSNP_6.

>
> 2. I would also like to plot a chosen CNV region to inspect the region
> as in the plot displayed here in your paper:
> http://bioinformatics.oxfordjournals.org/content/27/15/2038/F5.large.jpg.

That plot (Figure 5 from the Paired PSCBS paper in Olshen et al. 2011)
shows parent-specific CN estimates and segmentation results.  That is
possible to do from SNP arrays in the case that you have matched
normal (germline) samples for each tumor.  It is not clear from your
message if that is what you have and that is what you want to do.  It
sounds more like you wish to do a total CN analysis.  For total CN
plots, you can use the ChromosomeExplorer to generate PNG figures for
you, e.g.

sm <- CbsModel(ds);
ce <- ChromsomeExplorer(sm);
process(ce, verbose=-10);

This is illustrated in several of the other CN vignettes.

Hope this helps

/Henrik

> my_cellfile_1 and
> my_cellfile_2, to see the intensities and the segmentation. How would
> I do that?

messages.body_plain:
Dear Henrik,

I know my posting is not related to aroma.affymetrix, but I couldn't
find anyone but you that I can ask about this issue.
I am very sorry for the inconvenience I might have caused.

I urgently need to get tumor purity estimate for copy nrs from matched
tumor-normal pairs on the affymetrix snp6.0.
Even though I googled, I couldn't find a software that can estimate
tumor purity without an "error" for the platform.
ASCAT 2.0 (http://heim.ifi.uio.no/bioinf/Projects/ASCAT/) is not a
good candidate for my work, and I am looking for a different solution.
I wonder if you know a software for estimating tumor purity that you
have successfully run for your work.

Thank you very much,

Best,

Hk

messages.subject: NAs in FIRMA result matrix
messages.subject_clean: NAs in FIRMA result matrix
messages.body_plain:
Hello everybody,

I encountered some NA scores im my FIRMA results and I am not sure why
these occur. So far, I followed the instructions on the aroma website
and performed an RMA on all my samples using the binary CDF for my
Human Exon Array (http://www.aroma-project.org/chipTypes/HuEx-1_0-st-
v2).

Out of all probe sets, 4645 get NAs for all entries in the table,
though the expression matrix for these probe sets looks completely
fine (some examples are the probe sets 2377880, 2431529 and 2433240).
Is this a known bug or am I missing something in my code?
The other probe sets look good and I already picked up some
interesting genes, still I don't see why any NAs would be introduced.

Best regards,
Rene

=============================
CODE
=============================

chipType    = "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"    # specify the affymetrix chip type
we're using
cdf         = AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType(chipType,
tags="fullR3,A20071112,EP")
cs          = AffymetrixCelSet$byName("EMC_all", cdf=cdf)
setCdf(cs, cdf)

# RMA (BC + QN + SUM)

# BACKGROUND CORRECTION
    bc      = RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs, tag="fullR3")
    csBC    = process(bc,verbose=verbose)

# QUANTILE NORMALIZATION
    qn      = QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
    csN     = process(qn, verbose=verbose)

# FIT SUMMARY MODEL
    plmTr   = ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
    fit(plmTr, verbose=verbose) # run the model, this takes a while!
	cesTr = getChipEffectSet(plmTr)
    trFit = extractDataFrame(cesTr, units=NULL, addNames=TRUE)

    plmEx   = ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=FALSE)
    fit(plmEx, verbose=verbose) # run the model, this takes a while!
    cesEx   = getChipEffectSet(plmEx)
    ExFit   = extractDataFrame(cesEx, units=NULL, addNames=TRUE) #
this takes a while!

# Do FIRMA analysis
	firma       = FirmaModel(plmTr)
    fit(firma, verbose=verbose) # this takes a while!
    fs          = getFirmaScores(firma)
    fsScores    = extractDataFrame(fs)
    fsScores    = cbind(ExFit[,1:5],log2(fsScores[,-c(1:3)]))

Dear all,
I have used CbsModel() to generate segmentations. In the file
regions.xls it gives you segment location, mean and count. I have two
questions:

My 1st question is how can I generate GAIN/LOSS (1/-1) call for all
the markers using the result from CbsModel(), is there a function
available in the package?

Here is my idea of generating 1/-1 calls for the markers
         1.1)use student t test to test if the segment mean is
different from grand mean.

student t=(segment mean-grand mean)/sigma*sqrt(count)
grand mean=sum(mean*count)/sum(count)=  0.0156
Here is the segmentation result for subj1 chr 19. On the figure
sigma=0.206. I guess that is the std deviation for the raw copy number
on the whole chromosome.

sample	chr	start	stop	mean	count    ....... student t    ........GAIN/LOSS Call

Therefore two markers between 19957670 and 19958541 on chr19 are called -1.
         1.2)  freqency plot for segment means of the whole genome and
everybody in the reference group ( all the controls and cases are used
for reference), majority means will be around zero.
Find lower threshold and upper threshold to recode segment to -1 or 1.
Then the question is what is the optimal cutoff?

what do you think about these methods? Please give me some suggestion
on generating the GAIN/LOSS call from the CBS segmentation results.

My 2nd question is that I am only interested in a list of CNV markers,
is there a way to extract their intenstiy before and after
segmentation?

Thank you,
Qian

messages.body_plain:
Dear Pierre,

Thank you very much for your prompt reply.

FYI. I processed the Affymetrix SNP 6.0 data as follows:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
dataSet   <-"AffyTestData"
chipType  <-"GenomeWideSNP_6"
verbose     <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8, timestamp=TRUE);
cdf           <-AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType(chipType, tags="Full");
csR         <-AffymetrixCelSet$byName(dataSet, cdf=cdf);
ds           <- doCRMAv2(csR, cdf=cdf, combineAlleles=FALSE,
verbose=verbose);
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Then, I could access total and fracB data with the following scripts :
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
dsTotal     <- AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet$byName(dataSet, tags="ACC,ra,-
XY,BPN,-XY,AVG,FLN,-XY", chipType=chipType);
dsFracB    <- AromaUnitFracBCnBinarySet$byName(dataSet, tags="ACC,ra,-
XY,BPN,-XY,AVG,FLN,-XY", chipType=chipType)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

However, I couldn't access a chip effect set with:
cesN  <- CnChipEffectSet$byName(dataSet,tags="ACC,ra,-XY,BPN,-
XY,AVG,FLN,-XY", chipType=chipType)

And, as you know, it worked when I used "GenomeWideSNP_6.Full" as a
chip type:
cesN  <- CnChipEffectSet$byName(dataSet,tags="ACC,ra,-XY,BPN,-
XY,AVG,FLN,-XY", chipType=paste(chipType,",Full",sep=""))

Thank you,

Hoon

messages.body_plain:
Hoon, thanks for the note.  Yes, there is a discrepancy in how clever
the methods are.  Basically the AromaUnit<Nnn>CnBinarySet methods go
further in trying to figure out what annotations are needed.  FYI,
contrary to data set directories, the name of the chip type directory
will never have tags, which is why the files end up in:

plmData/AffyTestData,ACC,ra,-XY,BPN,-XY,AVG,FLN,-XY/GenomeWideSNP_6/

and not

plmData/AffyTestData,ACC,ra,-XY,BPN,-XY,AVG,FLN,-XY/GenomeWideSNP_6,Full/

regardless of CDF annotation you used  This was an active design
decision by us (which for various reasons would be too lengthy to get
into here).

To achieve some consistency with how you setup the AffymetrixCelSet, you can do:

dataSet <- "AffyTestData";
chipType <- "GenomeWideSNP_6";
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType(chipType, tags="Full");
csR <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName(dataSet, cdf=cdf);
cesN <- CnChipEffectSet$byName(dataSet,
tags="ACC,ra,-XY,BPN,-XY,AVG,FLN,-XY", cdf=cdf);

FYI, to speed up the latter, you can help out and specify arguments
'combineAlleles=FALSE' and 'mergeStrands=TRUE' (these correspond to
your doCRMAv2() call below).

/Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Dear aroma community,

We are trying to do paired CBS analysis on some Affy SNP 6.0 data
using the R package "PSCBS", but not sure how to extract the total CN
and BAF values from the raw array files (.CEL) into the needed format
(pasted below). It seems aroma.affymetrix has some relevant functions
but there are few examples to follow. Could someone provide some
sample code on this? Thanks!

              chromosome position        CT      betaT        CN
betaN
SNP_A-8575125          1   554484 1.8778996 0.06460427 1.8856720
0.1161352
SNP_A-8575115          1   554636 0.1659543 0.64621653 0.2282602
0.6919347

0.8425635
SNP_A-8709646          1   711153 1.3974123 0.25975011 2.2465997
0.1765471

CT: total tumor copy number
betaT:  tumor allele B fractions (BAFs)
CN: total matched normal copy number
betaN: matched normal BAFs

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I can reproduce this in a fresh R session, but only when running
outdated package versions.  So, please update:

source("http://aroma-project.org/hbLite.R");
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix");

DETAILS:

> library("aroma.core");

> ufl <- AromaUflFile$byChipType("Mapping250K_Sty", tags="na31,HB20101007");

> raw <- readRawFooter(ufl)$raw;
> xml <- rawToChar(raw);
> xmlList <- XML::xmlToList(xml);

Extra content at the end of the document
Error: 1: Extra content at the end of the document

Note how I had to to use the 'XML::' prefix.  If I do the following
and have aroma.core v2.3.0, it works:

> xmlList <- xmlToList(xml);

or equivalently

> xmlList <- aroma.core::xmlToList(xml);

It turns out that if you run an older aroma.core package prior to
v2.3.0 and/or that hasn't been built on R v2.14.0, there will be a
name clash for xmlToList() between the implementation in the
aroma.core package and the one in the XML package.

Lesson learned is to always make sure to run up-to-date versions of
packages and preferably R itself too.

/Henrik

The GenomeWideSNP_6 (and the GenomeWideSNP_5) chip is special, because
Affymetrix provides two different *annotation* sets (CDFs), one
"default" and one "full".

To use the "Full" annotation, you need the following annotation data files:

GenomeWideSNP_6,HB20080710.acs  (same for "default" and "full")
GenomeWideSNP_6,Full.cdf
GenomeWideSNP_6,Full,na31,hg19,HB20110328.ugp
GenomeWideSNP_6,Full,na31,hg19,HB20110328.ufl

and then do:

dataSet <- "TCGABreast";
chipType <- "GenomeWideSNP_6,Full";

csR <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName(dataSet, chipType=chipType);
...

/Henrik

On Wed, Nov 16, 2011 at 12:06 PM, Kai <wang...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Henrik,
>
> For GWS6 data it seems to me that they can be processed to generate
> either an "AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet" or a "CnChipEffectSet". For
> example, codes in your vignette "Estimation of total copy numbers
> using the CRMA v2 method" will produce a "CnChipEffectSet", whereas
> when one uses the "doCRMAv2" wrapper function it will produce an
> "AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet".

See how-to page 'Export total copy numbers and allele B fractions as
aroma binary data files':

  http://aroma-project.org/howtos/exportTotalAndFracB

for creating/exporting a CnChipEffectSet (a special case of
SnpChipEffectSet) to an AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet.

That is actually what is done in the last step of doCRMAv2(), cf.
print(doCRMAv2.AffymetrixCelSet).

An AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet data set can hold locus-specific total CN
estimates from any type of CN technology, e.g. Affymetrix, Illumina
and Agilent.   A CnChipEffectSet data set is customized for Affymetrix
only.  In the beginning (of the aroma framework), there we only dealt
with Affymetrix so CnChipEffectSet was natural but in order to bring
in other technologies to we came up with the technology-independent
AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet format.

(Maybe we should update those explicit CN vignettes to always do
exportTotalAndFracB() at the end.

>
> My question is whether these two data types are interchangeable? They
> don't seem able to be combined in downstream analysis such as
> CbsModel. The thing is that we processed the HAPMAP reference samples
> using "doCRMAv2" which produced an "AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet"; and
> recently we processed another dataset following the example in "http://

> However when we loaded both of them and tried to create a CbsModel
> using the pooled HAPMAP as reference, it failed.

I haven't tried to mix the two types and I didn't think of that use
case when extending the downstream methods to support that, so it may
not work. What is the error you get?  Either way, now you know how to
export to AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet, so you should be fine.

>
> Is there a way to convert the one object into the other?

As above.  There is no way implemented for going from an
AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet to a CnChipEffectSet.

> Or do we have
> to reprocess one dataset to generate the same type of object as the
> other?

So, the answer is no.

Hope this helps

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] hg18 or hg19 used in ChromosomeExplorer
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] hg18 or hg19 used in ChromosomeExplorer
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Wed, Nov 16, 2011 at 11:48 AM, Kai <wang...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Henrik,
>
> Is the ChromosomeExplorer able to tell which version of the reference
> genome was used in generating the copy number segments when drawing
> the chromosome plots? Or can it only display hg18 or hg19 but not
> both?

First, the location of the data points (=loci) are defined by the Unit
Genome Position (UGP) file associated with the CN data set.  In the
CRMA v2 pipeline, the UGP file is used already early on in the
preprocessing to infer which loci are on autosomal and which are on
sex chromosomes.  This is because we wish to *estimate* the
normalization functions (how we should normalize the data) such that
the normalization is independent of the composition of X and Y
chromosomes (read "the gender").  However, changing the UGP from an
hg18 to an hg19 one probably makes very little difference in the end
of the day to the CN estimates coming out of CRMAv2.

Second, the UGP is obviously used the segmentation step for lining up
the CN signals along the chromosomes.  So, if you move from hg18 to
hg19 this is very you should restart you process from.

>
> We are still processing some of our GWS6 data using the old hg18
> annotation, so I just want to make sure that the ChromosomeExplorer is
> displaying the right coordinates and cytobands.

The ChromosomeExplorer uses whatever UGP you segmentation model is
using to et the genomic locations of the loci.  Thus, if you change
UGP the loci will be plotted in at the new genomic locations.

The UGP annotation does *not* contain information about the cytobands.
 Instead that information is (supposed to be) retrieved from "genome"
annotation data under annotationData/genomes/<genomeName>/, where
<genomeName> is for instance 'Human' or 'Mouse'.  So by changing this
cytoband annotation file, you can change genome version.  If no file
is found, ChromosomeExplorer silently ignores it and no cytobands are
plotted.

Here I was supposed to explain how to change the cytoband annotation
file, but I realized that the aroma machinery for locating and parsing
such files is broken.  It has probably been broken for quite a while.
Thus, I expect that you right now don't get any cytobands in your
plots, unless you run a very old version of aroma.affymetrix in case
the cytobands according to the GLAD package are plotted, which means
that whatever version of cytobands GLAD uses is what is plotted.

So, (i) do you get cytobands, and (ii) what is your version of
aroma.affymetrix et al.?

I'll look into fixing the cytoband bug.

/Henrik

Here you are trying to concatenate copy number estimates for all
samples in a huge data.frame.
Remember that the SNP 6 array has roughly 2 million loci !  After 162
iterations, this data.frame has about 324 million lines !!!
It probably breaks down when your computer runs out of memory.

I see two problems here:
1) I don't think it's a good idea to try to create a text file with
228*2e6=456 million lines.  Why don't you create only one file per
sample ?  That would also be much easier to manipulate afterwards.
2) In case you'd really want to do that (again, I really don't see why
if you have that many samples), you should write the results to file
for each chromosome directly, using write.table(..., append=TRUE)
within the loop on index "j".  This way you would avoid using so much
memory, and also loosing a lot of time with this "rbind" which
re-creates a bigger and bigger data.frame at each iteration.

And my suggestion is: look at writeDataFrame: it should give you what
you need, see:

http://www.aroma-project.org/howtos/writeDataFrame

Cheers,

Pierre

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] TumorBoost and LOH
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] TumorBoost and LOH
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'd suggest that you use the Paired PSCBS segmentation method and the
LOH caller proposed in the PSCBS paper:

A.B. Olshen*, H. Bengtsson*, P. Neuvial, P. Spellman, R.A. Olshen,
V.E. Seshan, Parent-specific copy number in paired tumor-normal
studies using circular binary segmentation, Bioinformatics, 2011.
http://aroma-project.org/publications/

There is no high-level pipeline for doing this in the Aroma framework.
 We hope to get one up some day, but in the meanwhile, you can use the
PSCBS package directly as suggested in vignette 'Paired
parent-specific copy-number segmentation (Paired PSCBS) (low-level API
after AS-CRMAv2)':

  http://aroma-project.org/vignettes/PairedPSCBS-lowlevel

To call LOH after the segmentation step, just call callLOH(), but you
first also need to call allelic-balance (AB) via callAB(), so do
something like:

fit <- segmentByPairedPSCBS(df, verbose=verbose);
fit <- callAB(fit, verbose=verbose);
fit <- callLOH(fit, verbose=verbose);

and the columns 'abCall' and 'lohCall' (and a few others) will be
added to the table of segments.

BTW, by default Paired PSCBS will do TumorBoost for you (see above
article), so you don't have to do it explicitly.  However, since
you've already done it, you can let segmentByPairedPSCBS() know by
setting argument 'tbn=FALSE'.  However however, the above vignette
doesn't show how to extract the genotype calls nor the
TumorBoost-normalized BAFs, so it is probably just easier to start
with the signals before TumorBoost.

Hope this helps

Henrik

convert it into an AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet using the

On Nov 16, 5:09 pm, Henrik Bengtsson <henrik.bengts...@aroma-
project.org <http://project.org>> wrote:

> Hi.

>
> On Wed, Nov 16, 2011 at 12:06 PM, Kai <wangz...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi Henrik,
>
> > For GWS6 data it seems to me that they can be processed to generate
> > either an "AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet" or a "CnChipEffectSet". For
> > example, codes in your vignette "Estimation of total copy numbers
> > using the CRMA v2 method" will produce a "CnChipEffectSet", whereas
> > when one uses the "doCRMAv2" wrapper function it will produce an
> > "AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet".
>
> See how-to page 'Export total copy numbers and allele B fractions as
> aroma binary data files':
>
>  http://aroma-project.org/howtos/exportTotalAndFracB
>
> for creating/exporting a CnChipEffectSet (a special case of
> SnpChipEffectSet) to an AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet.
>
> That is actually what is done in the last step of doCRMAv2(), cf.
> print(doCRMAv2.AffymetrixCelSet).
>
> An AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet data set can hold locus-specific total CN
> estimates from any type of CN technology, e.g. Affymetrix, Illumina
> and Agilent.   A CnChipEffectSet data set is customized for Affymetrix
> only.  In the beginning (of the aroma framework), there we only dealt
> with Affymetrix so CnChipEffectSet was natural but in order to bring
> in other technologies to we came up with the technology-independent
> AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet format.
>
> (Maybe we should update those explicit CN vignettes to always do
> exportTotalAndFracB() at the end.
>
>
>
> > My question is whether these two data types are interchangeable? They
> > don't seem able to be combined in downstream analysis such as
> > CbsModel. The thing is that we processed the HAPMAP reference samples
> > using "doCRMAv2" which produced an "AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet"; and
> > recently we processed another dataset following the example in "http://
> >www.aroma-project.org/node/117 <http://www.aroma-project.org/node/117>" which produced a "CnChipEffectSet".
> > However when we loaded both of them and tried to create a CbsModel
> > using the pooled HAPMAP as reference, it failed.
>
> I haven't tried to mix the two types and I didn't think of that use
> case when extending the downstream methods to support that, so it may
> not work. What is the error you get?  Either way, now you know how to
> export to AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet, so you should be fine.
>
>
>
> > Is there a way to convert the one object into the other?
>
> As above.  There is no way implemented for going from an
> AromaUnitTotalCnBinarySet to a CnChipEffectSet.
>
> > Or do we have
> > to reprocess one dataset to generate the same type of object as the
> > other?
>
> So, the answer is no.
>
> Hope this helps
>
> /Henrik
>
>
>
> > Thanks very much for your help.
>
> > Best,
> > Kai

On Nov 16, 5:54 pm, Henrik Bengtsson <henrik.bengts...@aroma-
project.org <http://project.org>> wrote:
> Hi.

>
> On Wed, Nov 16, 2011 at 11:48 AM, Kai <wangz...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi Henrik,
>
> > Is the ChromosomeExplorer able to tell which version of the reference
> > genome was used in generating the copy number segments when drawing
> > the chromosome plots? Or can it only display hg18 or hg19 but not
> > both?
>
> First, the location of the data points (=loci) are defined by the Unit
> Genome Position (UGP) file associated with the CN data set.  In the
> CRMA v2 pipeline, the UGP file is used already early on in the
> preprocessing to infer which loci are on autosomal and which are on
> sex chromosomes.  This is because we wish to *estimate* the
> normalization functions (how we should normalize the data) such that
> the normalization is independent of the composition of X and Y
> chromosomes (read "the gender").  However, changing the UGP from an
> hg18 to an hg19 one probably makes very little difference in the end
> of the day to the CN estimates coming out of CRMAv2.
>
> Second, the UGP is obviously used the segmentation step for lining up
> the CN signals along the chromosomes.  So, if you move from hg18 to
> hg19 this is very you should restart you process from.
>
>
>
> > We are still processing some of our GWS6 data using the old hg18
> > annotation, so I just want to make sure that the ChromosomeExplorer is
> > displaying the right coordinates and cytobands.
>
> The ChromosomeExplorer uses whatever UGP you segmentation model is
> using to et the genomic locations of the loci.  Thus, if you change
> UGP the loci will be plotted in at the new genomic locations.
>
> The UGP annotation does *not* contain information about the cytobands.
>  Instead that information is (supposed to be) retrieved from "genome"
> annotation data under annotationData/genomes/<genomeName>/, where
> <genomeName> is for instance 'Human' or 'Mouse'.  So by changing this
> cytoband annotation file, you can change genome version.  If no file
> is found, ChromosomeExplorer silently ignores it and no cytobands are
> plotted.
>
> Here I was supposed to explain how to change the cytoband annotation
> file, but I realized that the aroma machinery for locating and parsing
> such files is broken.  It has probably been broken for quite a while.
> Thus, I expect that you right now don't get any cytobands in your
> plots, unless you run a very old version of aroma.affymetrix in case
> the cytobands according to the GLAD package are plotted, which means
> that whatever version of cytobands GLAD uses is what is plotted.
>
> So, (i) do you get cytobands, and (ii) what is your version of
> aroma.affymetrix et al.?
>
> I'll look into fixing the cytoband bug.
>
> /Henrik
>
>
>
> > Thanks in advance for your clarification.
>
> > Best,
> > Kai

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm digging through my inbox and found this one - sorry for wait.

On Tue, Oct 18, 2011 at 12:54 PM, rahul <v.rahul...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello Henrik,
>
>  I have a custom CDF for HuEx1.0stv2 and each probeset represents an
> exon. I am confused with mergeGroups option in ExonRmaPlm.
> When should we set mergeGrops=TRUE ? In my case since each probeset
> represents an exon, should i set the mergeGroups option to FALSE. I
> tried searching for documentation for ExonRmaPlm at "http://www.aroma-
> project.org <http://project.org>"and i did not find any. Can you please provide the
> reference file where ExonRmaPlm is explained.

It's not clear what you kind of analysis you want to do, but if you
look at the 'FIRMA - Human exon array analysis' vignette:

http://aroma-project.org/vignettes/FIRMA-HumanExonArrayAnalysis

you'll see that they use mergeGroups=FALSE for fitting each exon
independently, and mergeGroups=TRUE for fitting the all of them
together, that is, the transcript cluster.  With the latter approach,
when there is alternative splicing across your samples, then the model
is actually not representative and the exons that differ between
samples will end up getting large residuals in the model.  This is
what the authors of FIRMA [1] take advantage of for detecting
alternative splicing; in the above vignette you can see that they are
only using the mergeGroups=TRUE ('plmTr') model and that is what goes
into the FIRMA model at the end.

REFERENCES:
[1] E. Purdom, K. Simpson, M. Robinson, J. Conboy, A. Lapuk & T.P.
Speed, FIRMA: a method for detection of alternative splicing from exon
array data. Bioinformatics, 2008.

/Henrik

>
> Rahul

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] FIRMA on subset of normalized samples
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] FIRMA on subset of normalized samples
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Tue, Oct 18, 2011 at 2:46 AM, rene.rotterdam
<rene.boe...@googlemail.com> wrote:
> Hi everyone,
>
> in my group the question popped up whether it is possible to perform
> the FIRMA analysis on a subset of a number of samples that have been
> normalized all together.
> For example: Assume we have a data set of 6 different groups with
> different numbers of samples and we want to investigate differences in
> between 2 certain groups (e.g. control vs. treatment 1), would it be
> feasible to calculate the FIRMA scores just for the corresponding
> samples to make sure the scores are independent from the other
> samples?
> If I understand the FIRMA concept correctly it is not, as you pass the
> fitted model for all of the samples on to the fit function to
> calculate the scores, but I would like to be certain on that point.

There are two probe-level models (PLMs) in FIRMA.  The first one that
fits the ExonRmaPlm(..., mergeGroups=TRUE).  That is a multi-array
model which will give different estimates for a particular array if
you add or remove other samples.  There is also the concern that you
need enough samples in order for this PLM to work well.

The second PLM is the FirmaModel with operates on the *residuals* from
former model fit and calculates the FIRMA scores by averaging the
residuals per exon, cf. the following equation on Page 3 in [1]:

 F_ij = median_k \in exon j (r_ijk) / s

Unfortunately, there is also that 's' which is an estimate of the
standard deviation of the residuals, which is calculated across all
samples for that exon.   This means, if you ceteris paribus would add
or remove some arrays, the estimate of 's' would change.  As explained
in the paper, rescaling by the standard deviation is done for the
purpose of being able to compare across genes.  If that is not
important, then one could imagine running FirmaModel on a subset of
the arrays.

REFERENCES:
[1] E. Purdom, K. Simpson, M. Robinson, J. Conboy, A. Lapuk & T.P.
Speed, FIRMA: a method for detection of alternative splicing from exon
array data. Bioinformatics, 2008.

/Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi Michelle,

this is indeed an odd error.  There is something causing the reading
of one of the generated CEL files to fail, which I never seen before.
I have a few suspects, but first I need to know what you set up.

Q1. What does the following report:

library("aroma.affymetrix");
print(sessionInfo());

Q2. Assuming you still haven't deleted the problematic analysis, what
does the following report:

library("R.filesets");
path <- "probeData/TCGABreast,ACC,ra,-XY/GenomeWideSNP_6/";
filename <- "HAULS_p_TCGAb47_SNP_2N_GenomeWideSNP_6_C10_628454.CEL";
df <- GenericDataFile(filename, path=path);
print(df);
print(getChecksum(df));

Q3. If Q2 works, continue with:

library("affxparser");
hdr <- readCelHeader(getPathname(df));
str(hdr);

Q4. Are you working on a local hard disk or a shared/network file system?

Q5. If you retry doASCRMAv2() on the same pair, does the error remain?
 ...or is it a sporadic glitch?

Q6. You say "on some [arrays]" - do you by any chance run multiple
pairs in parallel on several machines?

DETAILS:

The error you get below seems to occur because readCel() in the
affxparser package fail to read the probe signals in the CEL file:

>         Reading probe signals...
> Unable to read file:
> probeData/TCGABreast,ACC,ra,-XY/GenomeWideSNP_6/HAULS_p_TCGAb47_SNP_2N_GenomeWideSNP_6_C10_628454.CEL
> Error in attr(cel, "row.names") <- seq_len(length(cel[[1]])) :
>   attempt to set an attribute on NULL
> In addition: Warning messages:
> 1: In log2(y) : NaNs produced
> 2: In log2(y) : NaNs produced
>         Reading probe signals...done

Oddly enough, readCel() does not throw an exception causing it to
interrupt the processing, but instead it silently returns as if it
actually read something.  The problematic CEL file obviously exists,
because there are lot of internal file tests before calling
affxparser's readCel().  Also, earlier, at the end of the cross-talk
calibration, aroma reports the CEL files name and also its internal
timestamp, which requires that the CEL file has been read (meaning it
can read something):

>     AffymetrixCelSet:
>     Name: TCGABreast
>     Tags: ACC,ra,-XY
>     Path: probeData/TCGABreast,ACC,ra,-XY/GenomeWideSNP_6
>     Platform: Affymetrix
>     Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_6,Full
>     Number of arrays: 2
>     Names: HAULS_p_TCGAb47_SNP_2N_GenomeWideSNP_6_C01_628430,
> HAULS_p_TCGAb47_SNP_2N_GenomeWideSNP_6_C10_628454 [2]
>     Time period: 2011-11-18 15:37:49 -- 2011-11-18 15:40:48
>     Total file size: 131.47MB
>     RAM: 0.00MB
>    CRMAv2/Allelic crosstalk calibration...done

My best guesses right now is that either (i) you are running OSX with
a corrupt affxparser (there's been some recent BioC report on that),
or (ii) you experience race conditions on a shared file system.
Though, as a collector of odd bugs, I'd like to learn something
different.

Cheers,

/Henrik

messages.subject: Identify outlier density curves by cel file ID, on density plots?
messages.subject_clean: Identify outlier density curves by cel file ID, on density plots?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Sorry if this is dumb, I am new to microarray analysis, and
aroma.affymetrix, and am having difficulties figuring out how data is
structured and how to access it.

I am working with 156 HG-U133a cel files and a csv file of patient
characteristics and outcomes (and a similar number of HG-U133 Plus2
chips).

Down the line I am hoping to be able to perform semi-supervised
expression data analysis, along the lines of the methods of Bair and
Tibshirani (2004, PLoS Biology p. 0511-0522), but for the moment am
attempting to examine my cel files, perform some QC and normalize my
datasets.

[I managed to create CDF and SAF files, and also  ACS and UPG files
(though I'm not sure if I have done this correctly). So far, I have
failed to create UFL files, but I don't think that I actually need
them, for my purposes?]

I have just figured out how to plot raw log2 probe signal density
plots colour coded by sample sub-type (by adapting code from
http://www.aroma-project.org/node/141 and /node/16), defined by SAF
file attribute values, but I would like to be able to identify
outlying probe signal density curves by CEL file ID on the plot.

Is there a way to do this, similar to R's identify function,
perhaps?

Thanks in advance for any assistance.

Kind regards

Anna Evans

Hi.

On Fri, Nov 25, 2011 at 10:07 AM, evansa <drann...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> Sorry if this is dumb, I am new to microarray analysis, and
> aroma.affymetrix, and am having difficulties figuring out how data is
> structured and how to access it.

If you have specific questions/use cases on accessing data, I'll try
to explain how to do it.  Some of the 'how to' pages contains useful
information how to retrieve array signals etc:

http://www.aroma-project.org/howtos/

>
> I am working with 156 HG-U133a cel files and a csv file of patient
> characteristics and outcomes (and a similar number of HG-U133 Plus2
> chips).
>
> Down the line I am hoping to be able to perform semi-supervised
> expression data analysis, along the lines of the methods of Bair and
> Tibshirani (2004, PLoS Biology p. 0511-0522), but for the moment am
> attempting to examine my cel files, perform some QC and normalize my
> datasets.
>
> [I managed to create CDF and SAF files, and also  ACS and UPG files
> (though I'm not sure if I have done this correctly). So far, I have
> failed to create UFL files, but I don't think that I actually need
> them, for my purposes?]

Affymetrix provides CDF files for the HG-U133A and the HG-U133_Plus_2
chip types so you should not have to create one yourself, unless you
wish to use special custom genome annotations.

An ACS file holds the cell (probe) sequences of a chip type.  That is
needed if you wish to do probe-sequence normalization, e.g.
BasePositionNormalization.

An UGP (not UPG) file contains genome location information for each
unit, which is only used for SNP/CN DNA analysis.  I doubt you want to
use that for your expression analysis.

The UFL file contains PCR fragment-length information for each unit,
i.e. how long each DNA fragment is that a unit ("gene") sits on after
been digested by the restriction enzymes.  This is used in the
FragmentLengthNormalization methods which was developed specifically
for DNA analysis.

It is not clear what your preprocessing pipeline is, but if you're
only doing plain RMA, you need neither of the ACS, UGP or UFL files.
The CDF alone (in addition to your SAF) should be enough.

>
> I have just figured out how to plot raw log2 probe signal density
> plots colour coded by sample sub-type (by adapting code from
> http://www.aroma-project.org/node/141 and /node/16), defined by SAF
> file attribute values, but I would like to be able to identify
> outlying probe signal density curves by CEL file ID on the plot.
>
> Is there a way to do this, similar to R's identify function,
> perhaps?

there exist no special solution for this "problem" - it is the same
issue have with plain R density plots, e.g.

x <- matrix(rnorm(1000), ncol=50);
plot(density(x[,1]), xlim=c(-5,5), ylim=c(0,0.8), main="", xlab="");
for (cc in 2:ncol(x)) lines(density(x[,cc]));

Just as identify() won't do anything for you here, it won't in aroma.

What you can do is to narrow down arrays of interest using different
color ('col') and line type ('lty') arguments as well as plotting only
a subset of arrays.  To do the latter, just extract a subset of the
arrays and pass that to plotDensity(), e.g.

csRs <- extract(csR, 51:60);
plotDensity(csRs);

Ideally one want a pipeline that "identifes" (read calls) arrays that
are outliers (have densities that stands out from the rest)
automatically and highlights them in the density plots as well as
lists their names.  This requires a density-curve outlier calling
algorithms - I am not aware of such a method.

/Henrik
